'''Trade Federation Basic''' was an [[Writing/Legends|alphabet]] and writing form of [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]]. The numbering system was used by the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] to identify individual [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|battle droids]].<ref name="Force Feedback">{{GamerCite|4|Force Feedback}}</ref> It was originally adapted from the written form of [[Pak Pak/Legends|Pak Pak]], the main [[Language/Legends|language]] of the [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidians]], when the latter were forced to learn Basic.<ref name="TWW">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/writtenword/index.html?page=1|text=The Written Word|int=The Written Word}}</ref>

==History==
===The Old Republic===
[[File:Neimoidian_Basic_crates.jpg|thumb|left|Cold War-era crates bearing inscriptions in Neimoidian Basic]]
The so-called Trade Federation Basic alphabet found its origin in the writing system of the [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidians]], a [[Near-Duros]] [[Species/Legends|species]] from [[Neimoidia/Legends|Neimoidia]]. Unlike their Duros ancestors, who spoke a [[Durese/Legends|phonetic language]], the Neimoidians had developed the [[Pak Pak/Legends|Pak Pak]], a new language made of modulated croaks. Because of that, the old Durese syllabary had become unusable, which prompted them to create a new writing system that could accurately express the sounds of Pak Pak. When the Neimoidians started with the wider galactic community, they realized their language was unspeakable by most offworlders, and they started learning [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]] while still using their own alphabet to transcribe it.<ref name="TWW" /> A form of that alphabet existed as early as of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]],<ref name="SWTOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> around [[3643 BBY]].<ref name="Time">{{TOR_dates|1}}</ref> At the time, inscriptions in Trade Federation Basic appeared on some crates that could be found on various locales, including [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Hutta]], [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] and [[Hammer Station]]. The text, however, featured some characters that did not correspond to later versions of the alphabet, and what could actually be deciphered reads as gibberish.<ref name="SWTOR" />

In [[350 BBY/Legends|350 BBY]],<ref name="TEGTAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> the Neimoidians were among the founding members of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], a shipping corporation and cartel.<ref name="E:ICS">''[[Star Wars: Episode I Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref> As [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] went by, their influence in the Federation became stronger and stronger, and their idiosyncratic script ended up being endorsed throughout the organization. Because of that, it was dubbed Trade Federation Basic from then on.<ref name="TWW" />

The alphabet followed the Federation's influence, and became known outside it. Technological firms that were signatories of the Federation, included this alphabet as default langauges in exported products.<ref name="TWW" />

The display on [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul's]] [[Macrobinoculars/Legends|macrobinoculars]] while searching for [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Amidala]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] showed Trade Federation Basic.<ref name="Episode I">{{Film|I}}</ref> 

When a Neimoidian activated the [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|Trade Federation Droid Army]] during the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]], Trade Federation Basic characters could be seen on the [[Computer/Legends|computer]] screen.<ref name="Episode I"/> 

The [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1 battle droids]] deployed by the Trade Federation in the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] had numerals written in Trade Federation Basic on their backpacks in a four digit format, including:<ref name="Episode I" />
*"[[1138 (Trade Federation)/Legends|1138]]," deactivated [[Droid/Legends|droid]] that fell limp before [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]] after the Trade Federation's [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|Droid Control Ship]] was destroyed.<ref name="Episode I" />
*"1234," shot down by Binks on the [[Great Grass Plains/Legends|Great Grass Plains]] with the [[E-5 blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifle]] of a cut in half battle droid.<ref name="Episode I" />
*"1373," "1472" and "2943," escorted a group of captives towards the [[Theed Royal Palace]].<ref name="Episode I" />
*"[[1933/Legends|1933]]," "[[2163/Legends|2163]]," "2767" and "7169," guarded the [[Naboo Royal Starship/Legends|Naboo Royal Starship]] and held members of the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Naboo Security Forces]] captive.<ref name="Episode I" />
**Curiously, ''another'' droid designated "2767" was lying fallen on the ground in front of a column after [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Quarsh Panaka/Legends|Panaka]] broke a large [[Window/Legends|window]] during the Battle of Naboo, while a ''third'' droid named "2767" was standing by one of the opposite columns.<ref name="Episode I" />
*"2296" and "2391," stationed on board the [[Saak'ak/Legends|''Saak'ak'']] while the [[Lucrehulk-class LH-3210 cargo freighter/Legends|freighter]] was part of the blockade of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].
*"2714" and "7824," fought against the [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]] at the [[Great Grass Plains/Legends|Great Grass Plains]].<ref name="Episode I" />
*"2724," tackled by one of Binks's fellow [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]]s while Bink's [[Limb/Legends|leg]] got stuck.<ref name="Episode I" />
*"3271," held a group of Gungans under captivity.<ref name="Episode I" />
*"6369," guarded the entrance to the Theed Royal Palace throne room.<ref name="Episode I" />
*"7276," forced Binks to surrender.<ref name="Episode I" />
*"7629," stood with their back to a large column after Panaka broke the window.<ref name="Episode I" />

A few years later, a monitor in the [[Eastport/Legends|Eastport]] processing station said "GATE 24."<ref name="Hnn-15 Dead in Houk / Weequay Brawl at Eastport">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|46|news/1337_4.html|15 Dead in Houk / Weequay Brawl at Eastport}}</ref>

===The Clone Wars===
During the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]], a [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droid]] that was firing at opposing [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] while [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] deflected a blaster shot into a [[OOM command battle droid/Legends|OOM command battle droid]], had "1138" printed on its booster pack.<ref name="Episode II">{{Film|II}}</ref>

Text in [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] blueprints was written with [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]] letters and Trade Federation Basic numbers. The blueprints of the temple [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]] included the text "AB281," "DELTA-7" and "[[Delta-7B Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|DELTA-7 AETHERSPRITE]]." The blueprints of the [[Analysis Rooms/Legends|Analysis Rooms]] include "FLOOR 47" and "3263827 ANALYSIS." The specifications of the [[SP-4 analysis droid/Legends|Sp-4 analysis droid]] includes the text "IC-GR8 ANALYSIS DROID."<ref name="Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Attack of the Clones">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Attack of the Clones]]''</ref>

[[File:Sep-script-thecitadel.png|thumb|200px|Trade Federation Basic on Separatist computer screens.]]
The [[T-series tactical droid/Legends|T-series tactical droid]] has the letter L on its chest.<ref name="The Hidden Enemy">{{TCW|The Hidden Enemy}}</ref> One version also had the letter on its head.<ref name="The Gungan General">{{TCW|The Gungan General}}</ref>

During the [[Battle of Lola Sayu/Legends|mission to the citadel]], a tactical droid's computer screen read "[[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|SEPARATIST]] [[Class type B/Legends|ESCORT SHUTTLE CLASS TYPE B]]" • "SCAN COMPLETE" • "SUPPLIES" • "BEVERAGES" • "[[Foodstuff/Legends|FOOD]]" • "MORE FOOD" • "[[Blaster/Legends|GUNS]]" • "GENERAL SUPPLIES" • "FROZEN RATIONS" • "[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|ANAKIN SKYWA]]<small>''[obscured]''</small>" • "[[Carbonite/Legends|CARBONITE]]" • "METAL." The bottom of the screen contained the options "DESTROY" and "LET PASS."<ref name="The Citadel">{{TCW|The Citadel (episode)}}</ref>

While [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] was looking into the [[Bombing of the Jedi Temple hangar/Legends|bombing of the Jedi Temple hangar]] and conversing with [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]] in the [[Coruscant Underworld/Legends|Coruscant underworld]],<ref name="The Wrong Jedi">{{TCW|The Wrong Jedi}} {{C|the top of the sign begins with the letters "CA" and the bottom ends with the letters "TO" — the name "[[Cato (Coruscant)/Legends|Cato]]" is confirmed in the {{SW|url=series/clone-wars/to-catch-a-jedi-concept-art-gallery|text="To Catch a Jedi" Concept Art Gallery}} {{C|slide 6}}}}</ref> a prominent sign for a dancing establishment<ref name="Catch">{{TCW|To Catch a Jedi}}</ref> on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant's]] [[Level 1312/Legends|Level 1312]] displayed Trade Federation Basic. It said "[[Cato (Coruscant)/Legends|CATO]]."<ref name="The Wrong Jedi" />

Toward the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Trade Federation Basic was seen on the monitors of [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]]' [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']], as Captain [[Lushros Dofine/Legends|Lushros Dofine]] said, "[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Two]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Jedi]] have landed in the main [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]] bay. We're tracking them."<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith">{{Film|III}}</ref>

===Imperial Era===
After the Federation was nationalized by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], usage of the alphabet declined, and was limited to the worlds that were former members of the Federation, and of course the native Neimoidians.<ref name="TWW" />
